author: ojiudezue
title: Envoy: upstream fix does not close our path; MQTT local stream is trusted-independent but can read FRESH-yet-WRONG after an Envoy reboot; Emporia stays solar-follow primary permanently
summary: EnvoyClientClosedError subclasses RuntimeError, not EnvoyError, so HA's handler still leaks it — the 'wait for 2026.9.4' plan is retracted. The MQTT stream measured stream-up 99.78% of native-down time (run 1, 2.4 h clean). During the operator's Envoy reboot it reported a PARTIAL fleet (devices 48->8) so SOC read 87->20 with the battery ~90% — fresh timestamps, wrong value. Operator ruled Emporia the permanent solar-follow primary ('I trust emporia more period'); stream = fallback only.
why: Freshness alone is insufficient for a SOC tier: completeness (all 8 battery units) and a physical slew bound are required. Trust over speed was an explicit operator ruling even though the Emporia/Envoy gap is mostly the 1-min average lagging.
implications: ENVOY-STREAM-SOC-TIER-1 must carry the device-completeness + slew guard; B2/B3 (stream as primary, tighter freshness) are dropped, do not re-propose. Trust run 2 due >= 2026-09-26 20:15 over a clean 24 h window.
revisit_trigger: Revisit the stream-as-SOC-tier only after run 2 closes stream-vs-native agreement and the reserve witness.
